newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samchully to privately place convertibles.
newsitem.headline: Samchully to privately place convertibles.

text.p: South Korea's Samchully Corp said on Wednesday it would privately place 30 billion won worth of convertible bonds to raise operation funds.
The bonds, with a 10 percent coupon and due to mature on December 31, 2002, will guarantee an 11 percent annual yield, a company statement said.
The bonds can be converted into common Samchully shares one month after the issuing date until December 31, 2002. Conversion price was set at 64,000 won.
Samchully shares closed on Wednesday 63,000, down 1,000.
Daishin Life Insurance agreed to underwrite 20 billion won worth of bonds and Samsung Life Insurance the rest.
